peer_results.rationale: The available candidates for Bank of America focus on the definition of 'covered positions' which are intended for a 'short-term horizon' (bac_2024_7_P410_S003) or general trading risk factors (bac_2024_7_D324). These do not substantively compare to Citi's specific disclosure regarding the one-year stress testing horizon or the specific two-month exception for crisis-era liquidity; the BAC disclosures describe the composition of VaR inputs rather than the specific time-horizon methodology for stress testing market values.

comparisons.peer_summary: Corporate Treasury measures EaR over a one-year horizon following 100- and 200-basis point instantaneous parallel shocks in interest rates relative to a baseline scenario. Models incorporate contractual elements, balance sheet composition assumptions, prepayment behavior, and deposit repricing calibrated using historical behavior and competitive landscape, with continuous monitoring of key assumptions.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Goldman Sachs (GS) utilize a one-year time horizon for a significant portion of their market risk stress testing and economic risk measurements. Citi defines general changes in market values over a one-year horizon (c_2024_7_P556_S001), while GS measures its Economic at Risk (EaR) over a one-year time horizon following interest rate shocks (gs_2024_7_P377_S002). This indicates a shared standard for longer-term structural risk assessment, distinct from the shorter horizons used for highly liquid trading positions.

sentences.text: In general, changes in market values are defined over a one-year horizon.
We measure EaR over a one-year time horizon following a 100- and 200-basis point instantaneous parallel shock in both short- and long-term interest rates.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR) is a liquidity requirement measuring the adequacy of available stable funding over a one-year horizon. For the three months ended December 31, 2024, both the Firm and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. were compliant with the 100% minimum NSFR requirement.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and JPMorgan Chase reference a one-year horizon in the context of financial stability and liquidity adequacy, although for different specific measures. Citi uses a one-year horizon to define general changes in market values for stress testing (c_2024_7_P556_S001). Similarly, JPMorgan defines the Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR) as a requirement measuring stable funding adequacy over a one-year horizon (jpm_2024_7_P420_S001). Both firms anchor critical risk and liquidity metrics to this one-year timeframe.

sentences.text: In general, changes in market values are defined over a one-year horizon.

The net stable funding ratio ("NSFR") is a liquidity requirement for large banking organizations that is intended to measure the adequacy of "available" stable funding that is sufficient to meet their "required" amounts of stable funding over a one-year horizon.

peer_results.rationale: The available candidates for Morgan Stanley focus on Value-at-Risk (VaR) parameters, specifically a one-day time horizon and 95% confidence level (ms_2024_7_D247, ms_2024_7_D246). This contrasts with Citi's disclosure which centers on a one-year horizon for general stress testing. While both relate to time horizons, the specific metric (VaR vs. Stress Testing/EaR) and the horizon (one-day vs. one-year) are fundamentally different measurements, making the MS candidates not sufficiently comparable to Citi's specific topic of one-year stress testing horizons.
